note: Shared conformance corpus for the JSON-Schema `hostname` format (RFC 1123 / RFC 952 ASCII host names). Each entry has an id, an `instance` (the string under test), a `valid` boolean (the PINNED generator-owned verdict), and a human `why`. The pinned check = a single RE2-safe regex (labels of [A-Za-z0-9-], 1-63 chars, no leading/trailing '-', separated by '.', at least one label, case-insensitive) PLUS a cheap total-length guard (1..=253 chars). Trailing dot is REJECTED (matches JSON-Schema-Test-Suite draft2020-12 section 1). All-numeric labels/TLD are ACCEPTED (RFC 1123's 'never #.#.#.#' note is not enforced syntactically -- documented residual). A-label/IDNA validation (xn-- Punycode decoding, the test-suite's section-2 cases) is OUT OF SCOPE -- that is idn-hostname; an xn-- label here is just an ordinary LDH label. Total length is checked OUTSIDE the regex (RE2 has no lookahead), which is portable in every target. Corpus is applied only to string instances; the JSON-Schema 'ignore non-strings' rows are a validator-integration concern, not a check-of-the-string concern, so they are not in this string corpus.
